A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of ZnO, the resistance is the key factor to determine the field emission performance of ZnO emitters.
the conductivity of the emitter should be as high as possible and uniform as much as possible.
the resistance of the ZnO nanostructures should be reduced to the lowest possible value in the design and fabrication of ZnO nanostructures for device applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the field emission device, the emitter with low resistance is more likely to be the first emitter that emits, while the emitter with high resistance is more likely the last emitter that emits.
, for a given ZnO nanostructure type, the field emission performance of an array can be optimized by choosing the ZnO nanostructures with the best conductivity.
